description: Figure 5 (right panel) illustrates the sparsity ratio of SDPA output values across layers under a threshold of 1e-3, showing three curves for different gating-related measurements. The x-axis is labeled “Layer,” uses a linear scale, and spans approximately 0 to 23 with tick labels at regular intervals of 5 (0, 5, 10, 15, 20). The y-axis is labeled “Sparsity Ratio,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 0.0 up to about 0.8 with tick labels at 0.2 increments (0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8). A blue dashed line (legend: “sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.003”) stays very close to zero across all layers, starting near 0 at layer 0 and remaining near 0 through the final layer. An orange dashed line (legend: “sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.126”) starts high near about 0.75 at layer 0, drops steeply over the first several layers (falling below ~0.1 by around layer 5), and then approaches near-zero values for mid-to-late layers, with a small uptick near the end (around layers ~21–23) reaching roughly ~0.05–0.08 at the last layer. A green dash-dot line (legend: “sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.080”) also begins high near about 0.75 at layer 0, declines rapidly (to around ~0.1 by roughly layer 4–5), and then continues decreasing toward near zero, staying close to 0 for later layers with only minimal variation through the final layer.
